# modal.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/modal.mdx

title: Modal
description: A fully accessible modal dialog that uses the native dialog element with proper focus management and keyboard interactions.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Modal } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The Modal component provides a dialog window that appears on top of the main content. It uses the native HTML `<dialog>` element for built-in accessibility features and includes smooth transitions, focus management, and keyboard interactions.

<Aside type="note" title="View transitions">
  The component automatically handles Astro's view transitions.

## When to use

The Modal component is perfect for situations where you need to capture user attention:

- Confirmation dialogs
- Important notifications
- Form submissions
- Image galleries
- Terms and conditions
- Cookie consent notices
- User feedback prompts

<Aside type="caution" title="Use sparingly">
  Modals can be disruptive to the user experience. Only use them when you need the user's immediate attention or action.

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <button id="modal-example-trigger" class="sl-button variant-accent">Open Modal Example</button>
  
  <Modal
    triggerId="modal-example-trigger"
    title="Welcome to the Modal Component"
  >
    <p>This is a simple example of the Modal component.</p>
    <p>Try using the <kbd>Escape</kbd> key to close it, or click the X button.</p>
    <p>The modal maintains focus within itself while open and returns focus to the trigger button when closed.</p>
  </Modal>

## Usage

Learn how to implement the Modal component in your project, from basic usage to advanced configurations.

### Basic

```astro
---
import { Modal } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<button id="modal-trigger">Open Modal</button>

<Modal
  triggerId="modal-trigger"
  title="Welcome!"
>
  <p>This is the modal content.</p>
</Modal>
```

### With custom close action

```astro
<Modal 
  triggerId="modal-action"
  title="Confirm action"
  closeText="Cancel"
>
  <p>Are you sure you want to continue?</p>
  <button onclick="closeModal()">Confirm</button>
</Modal>
```

<Aside type="tip" title="Global close function">
  Use the global `closeModal()` function in your own buttons or callbacks to programmatically close the modal.

## Props

Configure the Modal component using these available props to customize its behavior and appearance.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `triggerId` | `string` | - | ID of the button that triggers the modal |
| `title` | `string` | - | Title text for the modal header |
| `headingSize` | `string` | `'h2'` | The visual size of the title element |
| `closeText` | `string` | `'Close'` | Text for the close button |
| `closeIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | Show/hide the close icon |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Accessibility

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component through native HTML elements and careful consideration of user interactions. The Modal component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Native `<dialog>` element with built-in accessibility
- Focus management
  - Focus trapped inside modal
  - Returns focus to trigger on close
- Keyboard support
  - Escape to close
  - Tab/Shift+Tab navigation
- ARIA attributes and semantic structure
- Smooth transitions with reduced-motion support

## Styling

Make the Modal component your own with custom styling while maintaining its accessibility features.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When customizing styles, ensure you maintain sufficient color contrast ratios and don't remove focus indicators or other accessibility features.

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    /* Option 1: Using :global() in your style block */
    <style>
      :global(.modal) {
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        border: 1px solid light-dark(hsl(204 20% 88%), hsl(215 25% 27%));
        background: light-dark(hsl(0 0% 100%), hsl(215 25% 15%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
        box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.1);
      }

      :global(.modal-inner) {
        padding: 1.5rem;
      }

      :global(.modal h3) {
        margin-block-start: 0;
        font-size: 1.25rem;
      }

      :global(.modal-close button) {
        padding: 0.5rem;
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 8% 45%), hsl(215 8% 65%));
      }

      :global(.modal-close button:hover) {
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
      }

      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
        :global(.modal[open]) {
          animation: fade-in 0.2s ease-out;
        }
      }
    </style>

    /* Option 2: Using is:global on the style tag */
    <style is:global>
      .modal {
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        border: 1px solid light-dark(hsl(204 20% 88%), hsl(215 25% 27%));
        background: light-dark(hsl(0 0% 100%), hsl(215 25% 15%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
        box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.1);
      }

      .modal-inner {
        padding: 1.5rem;
      }

      .modal h3 {
        margin-block-start: 0;
        font-size: 1.25rem;
      }

      .modal-close button {
        padding: 0.5rem;
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 8% 45%), hsl(215 8% 65%));
      }

      .modal-close button:hover {
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
      }

      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
        .modal[open] {
          animation: fade-in 0.2s ease-out;
        }
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <Modal 
      triggerId="modal-custom"
      title="Custom Modal"
      class="rounded-lg border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-100 shadow-lg"
    >
      <div class="p-6">
        <p class="text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-300">
          Modal content with Tailwind styling
        </p>
      </div>
    </Modal>
    ```

<Aside type="note" title="Style scoping">
  Astro components use scoped styles by default. To override component styles, you'll need to use either `:global()` selectors or the `is:global` directive on your style tag.

## Interactive examples

See the Modal component in action with these practical examples.

### Default modal

<button id="modal1-trigger" class="button">Open modal</button>

<div class="not-content">
  <Modal triggerId="modal1-trigger" title="Welcome">
    <p>This is a basic modal example with default settings.</p>
  </Modal>

### With custom close action

<button id="modal2-trigger" class="button">Confirm action</button>

<div class="not-content">
  <Modal triggerId="modal2-trigger" title="Are you sure?" closeText="Cancel">
    <p>This modal includes a custom close action.</p>
    <button class="button" onclick="closeModal()">Confirm</button>
  </Modal>

# notification.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/notification.mdx

title: Notification
description: A fully accessible notification component for displaying status messages, alerts, and feedback to users.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Notification } from 'accessible-astro-components';
import { Icon } from 'astro-icon/components';

## Introduction

The Notification component provides a way to display important messages to users with different severity levels and proper ARIA attributes for accessibility. It supports various types of notifications and can be enhanced with icons.

## When to use

Use notifications to display important messages that require user attention or acknowledgment. Common use cases include:

- Status updates
- Success messages
- Warning alerts
- Error messages
- Information notices
- System feedback
- Form submission results

Each type of notification has a specific purpose:
- **Info**: For general information and neutral updates
- **Success**: To confirm successful actions or positive outcomes
- **Warning**: For potential issues that need attention
- **Error**: To indicate critical problems or failed actions
- **Default**: For general messages that don't fit other categories

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification type="info" role="status">
    <Icon name="ion:information-circle-outline" size="1.5rem" />
    <p><strong>Info:</strong> Try different notification types below!</p>
  </Notification>
  
  <div style="margin-top: 1rem;">
    <Notification type="success" role="status">
      <Icon name="ion:checkbox-outline" size="1.5rem" />
      <p><strong>Success:</strong> Your action was completed successfully.</p>
    </Notification>
  
  <div style="margin-top: 1rem;">
    <Notification type="warning" role="status">
      <Icon name="ion:warning-outline" size="1.5rem" />
      <p><strong>Warning:</strong> Please review before proceeding.</p>
    </Notification>

<Aside type="tip" title="Dynamic notifications">
  When adding notifications dynamically (after user interaction), use `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` to inform screen reader users.

## Usage

Learn how to implement the Notification component in your project, from basic usage to advanced configurations.

```astro ins={13}
---
import { Notification } from 'accessible-astro-components'
import { Icon } from 'astro-icon/components'
---

<!-- Basic notification -->
<Notification>
  <p><strong>Message:</strong> This is a notification.</p>
</Notification>

<!-- With icon and type -->
<Notification type="info" role="status">
  <Icon name="ion:information-circle-outline" />
  <p><strong>Info:</strong> This is an info notification.</p>
</Notification>
```

### Accent variant (automatic icons)

The accent variant includes automatic icons and sleek styling - no manual icon management needed!

```astro
<!-- Accent notifications with automatic icons -->
<Notification type="success" variant="accent" role="status">
  <p><strong>Success:</strong> Your file has been uploaded!</p>
</Notification>

<Notification type="warning" variant="accent" role="status">
  <p><strong>Warning:</strong> Storage space is running low.</p>
</Notification>

<Notification type="error" variant="accent" role="alert">
  <p><strong>Error:</strong> Failed to connect to server.</p>
</Notification>
```

<Aside type="note" title="Icon integration">
  The default variant examples use [Astro Icon](https://github.com/natemoo-re/astro-icon) for manual icons, but the accent variant includes automatic icons for all notification types.

## Props

Configure the Notification component using these available props to customize its behavior and appearance.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'default'` | `'default'` | Sets the notification style and context |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'accent'` | `'default'` | Visual style variant of the notification |
| `element` | `'div' \| 'aside'` | `'div'` | Semantic element to use for the notification |
| `role` | `'none' \| 'alert' \| 'log' \| 'marquee' \| 'status' \| 'timer' \| 'region'` | `'none'` | ARIA role for the notification |
| `message` | `string` | `'This is a notification!'` | Default message when no children are provided |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Accessibility

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component through semantic HTML elements and proper ARIA attributes. The Notification component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Semantic `<aside>` element for complementary content
- Proper ARIA roles for dynamic content
- High contrast colors meeting WCAG guidelines
- Contextual information through clear labeling
- Screen reader announcements for dynamic notifications

## Styling

Make the Notification component your own with custom styling while maintaining its accessibility features.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When customizing styles, ensure you maintain sufficient color contrast ratios and don't remove focus indicators or other accessibility features.

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    /* Option 1: Using :global() in your style block */
    <style>
      :global(.notification) {
        display: flex;
        gap: 1rem;
        padding: 1rem;
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        border-inline-start: 4px solid;
        background: light-dark(hsl(204 20% 94%), hsl(215 25% 15%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(215 8% 45%), hsl(215 8% 65%));
      }

      :global(.notification[data-type="info"]) {
        background: light-dark(hsl(198 100% 94%), hsl(234 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(200 96% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(200 78% 46%), hsl(234 100% 60%));
      }

      :global(.notification[data-type="success"]) {
        background: light-dark(hsl(142 72% 94%), hsl(142 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(142 76% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(142 78% 46%), hsl(142 100% 60%));
      }

      :global(.notification[data-type="warning"]) {
        background: light-dark(hsl(48 100% 94%), hsl(48 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(48 96% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(48 78% 46%), hsl(48 100% 60%));
      }

      :global(.notification[data-type="error"]) {
        background: light-dark(hsl(0 100% 94%), hsl(0 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(0 96% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(0 78% 46%), hsl(0 100% 60%));
      }
    </style>

    /* Option 2: Using is:global on the style tag */
    <style is:global>
      .notification {
        display: flex;
        gap: 1rem;
        padding: 1rem;
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        border-inline-start: 4px solid;
        background: light-dark(hsl(204 20% 94%), hsl(215 25% 15%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(215 8% 45%), hsl(215 8% 65%));
      }

      .notification[data-type="info"] {
        background: light-dark(hsl(198 100% 94%), hsl(234 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(200 96% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(200 78% 46%), hsl(234 100% 60%));
      }

      .notification[data-type="success"] {
        background: light-dark(hsl(142 72% 94%), hsl(142 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(142 76% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(142 78% 46%), hsl(142 100% 60%));
      }

      .notification[data-type="warning"] {
        background: light-dark(hsl(48 100% 94%), hsl(48 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(48 96% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(48 78% 46%), hsl(48 100% 60%));
      }

      .notification[data-type="error"] {
        background: light-dark(hsl(0 100% 94%), hsl(0 54% 20%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(0 96% 27%), hsl(0 0% 100%));
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(0 78% 46%), hsl(0 100% 60%));
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <Notification 
      type="info"
      class="flex gap-4 p-4 rounded-lg border-l-4 bg-blue-50 dark:bg-blue-900 text-blue-900 dark:text-white border-blue-500"
    >
      <Icon name="ion:information-circle-outline" size="1.5rem" />
      <p>Notification content with Tailwind styling</p>
    </Notification>
    ```

<Aside type="note" title="Style scoping">
  Astro components use scoped styles by default. To override component styles, you'll need to use either `:global()` selectors or the `is:global` directive on your style tag.

## Interactive examples

See the Notification component in action with these practical examples:

### Default notification

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification>
    <p><strong>Message:</strong> This is a notification.</p>
  </Notification>

### Info notification

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification type="info" role="status">
    <Icon name="ion:information-circle-outline" size="1.5rem" />
    <p><strong>Info:</strong> This is a notification of type info.</p>
  </Notification>

### Success notification

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification type="success" role="status">
    <Icon name="ion:checkbox-outline" size="1.5rem" />
    <p><strong>Success:</strong> This is a notification of type success.</p>
  </Notification>

### Warning notification

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification type="warning" role="status">
    <Icon name="ion:warning-outline" size="1.5rem" />
    <p><strong>Warning:</strong> This is a notification of type warning.</p>
  </Notification>

### Error notification

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification type="error" role="alert">
    <Icon name="ion:alert-circle-outline" size="1.5rem" />
    <p><strong>Error:</strong> This is a notification of type error.</p>
  </Notification>

### Accent variant notifications

The accent variant provides a sleek design with automatic icons and a beautiful left border accent. Perfect for modern interfaces!

<div class="not-content">
  <Notification type="info" variant="accent" role="status">
    <p><strong>Info:</strong> This accent notification automatically includes an icon and styled border.</p>
  </Notification>

    <Notification type="success" variant="accent" role="status">
      <p><strong>Success:</strong> Your changes have been saved successfully!</p>
    </Notification>

    </Notification>

    <Notification type="error" variant="accent" role="alert">
      <p><strong>Error:</strong> Something went wrong. Please try again.</p>
    </Notification>
  
  <div style="margin-top: 1rem;">
    <Notification variant="accent">
      <p><strong>Default:</strong> A neutral accent notification for general messages.</p>
    </Notification>

# overview.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/overview.mdx

title: Overview
description: A collection of accessible components ready to enhance your Astro website.

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Introduction

The [Accessible Astro Components](https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-components) is a collection of accessible components built for Astro. Each component follows WAI-ARIA guidelines and best practices for accessibility. All components are build using the `light-dark()` function to ensure they are accessible in both light and dark mode.

## Installation

  <TabItem label="npm">
    ```bash
    npm install accessible-astro-components
    ```
  <TabItem label="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm add accessible-astro-components
    ```
  <TabItem label="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn add accessible-astro-components
    ```

## Available Components

- **Accordion**: Expandable/collapsible sections for progressive disclosure
- **Avatar**: User or entity representation with support for images, initials, and fallbacks
- **AvatarGroup**: Display multiple avatars in condensed or grid layouts
- **Badge**: Compact way to display status information, labels, or counts
- **Breadcrumbs**: Navigation aid showing the current page's location
- **Card**: Content container with flexible layout options
- **DarkMode**: Theme toggle with system preference support
- **Media**: Responsive image component
- **Modal**: Accessible dialog windows
- **Notification**: Info and alert messages
- **Pagination**: Navigation for paginated content
- **SkipLinks**: Keyboard navigation aid for screen readers
- **Tabs**: Content organization with tabbed interfaces
- **Video**: YouTube embed component

Each component is documented individually with its props, usage examples, and accessibility features.

---

# pagination.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/pagination.mdx

title: Pagination
description: A fully accessible pagination component for navigating through multi-page content with proper ARIA labels and keyboard support.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Pagination } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The Pagination component provides a navigation system for multi-page content with first, previous, next, and last page controls. It's built with accessibility in mind, featuring proper ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and clear visual states.

## When to use

Use the Pagination component when you need to split content across multiple pages:

- Blog post listings
- Search results
- Product catalogs
- Image galleries
- Data tables
- Long form content

<Aside type="tip" title="Progressive enhancement">
  The component automatically disables navigation controls when no valid URL is provided, ensuring a good user experience even at page boundaries.

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <p>Try using Tab key to navigate through the pagination controls:</p>
  <div style="margin-top: 1rem;">
    <Pagination
      firstPage="#"
      previousPage="#"
      nextPage="#"
      lastPage="#"
      currentPage={3}
      totalPages={5}
    />
  <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.9rem;">Notice how each control has a clear focus state and descriptive ARIA labels.</p>

## Usage

Learn how to implement the Pagination component in your project, from basic usage to advanced configurations.

### Basic

```astro
---
import { Pagination } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Pagination
  firstPage="/blog/1"
  previousPage="/blog/4"
  nextPage="/blog/6"
  lastPage="/blog/12"
  currentPage="5"
  totalPages="12"
  ariaLabel="Blog navigation"
/>
```

### Custom progress text

```astro
---
import { Pagination } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Pagination
  currentPage="5"
  totalPages="12"
  renderProgress={({ currentPage, totalPages }) =>
    `${currentPage} of ${totalPages} pages`
  }
/>
```

<Aside type="note" title="Custom progress text">
  You can customize the progress text using the `renderProgress` prop. It's a function that receives the current page and total pages as arguments and returns a string.

### Custom labels (simple)

For simple label customization (like internationalization), use the individual label props:

```astro
---
import { Pagination } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Pagination
  currentPage="5"
  totalPages="12"
  firstPageLabel="Zur ersten Seite"
  previousPageLabel="Zur vorherigen Seite"
  nextPageLabel="Zur nächsten Seite"
  lastPageLabel="Zur letzten Seite"
/>
```

<Aside type="tip" title="Internationalization">
  Individual label props are perfect for i18n - just pass translated strings without writing custom functions.

### Custom labels (advanced)

For dynamic label generation with page numbers or complex logic, use the `renderPageLabel` function:

```astro
---
import { Pagination } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Pagination
  currentPage="5"
  totalPages="12"
  renderPageLabel={({ type, page }) => {
    switch (type) {
      case 'first':
        return `Navigate to first page (page 1)`
      case 'previous':
        return `Navigate to previous page (page ${page})`
      case 'next':
        return `Navigate to next page (page ${page})`
      case 'last':
        return `Navigate to last page (page ${page})`
    }
  }}
/>
```

<Aside type="note" title="Advanced customization">
  The `renderPageLabel` function receives `type` and `page` parameters, allowing you to include specific page numbers or implement complex labeling logic. When provided, it overrides the individual label props.

## Props

Configure the Pagination component using these available props to customize its behavior and appearance.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `firstPage` | `string \| null \| undefined` | `'#'` | URL for the first page, falsy value disables the control |
| `previousPage` | `string \| null \| undefined` | `'#'` | URL for the previous page, falsy value disables the control |
| `nextPage` | `string \| null \| undefined` | `'#'` | URL for the next page, falsy value disables the control |
| `lastPage` | `string \| null \| undefined` | `'#'` | URL for the last page, falsy value disables the control |
| `currentPage` | `string \| number` | `'1'` | Current page number |
| `totalPages` | `string \| number` | `'12'` | Total number of pages |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `'Pagination'` | Accessible label for the navigation |
| `firstPageLabel` | `string` | `'Go to the first page'` | Accessible label for the first page button |
| `previousPageLabel` | `string` | `'Go to the previous page'` | Accessible label for the previous page button |
| `nextPageLabel` | `string` | `'Go to the next page'` | Accessible label for the next page button |
| `lastPageLabel` | `string` | `'Go to the last page'` | Accessible label for the last page button |
| `renderProgress` | `Function` | See example | Custom function to render the progress text |
| `renderPageLabel` | `Function` | See example | Custom function to generate accessible labels (overrides individual label props) |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Accessibility

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component through semantic HTML elements and proper ARIA attributes. The Pagination component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Semantic `<nav>` element with descriptive `aria-label`
- Clear visual indication of disabled controls
- Descriptive ARIA labels combining both context and page numbers (e.g., "Go to next page (page 6)")
- Keyboard navigation support
- High contrast icons and text
- Clear focus indicators
- Proper disabled states

<Aside type="tip" title="Screen readers">
  The component uses descriptive ARIA labels like "Go to first page" to ensure clear navigation for screen reader users.

## Styling

<Aside type="caution" title="Maintain accessibility">
  When customizing styles, ensure you maintain sufficient color contrast ratios and don't remove focus indicators or other accessibility features.

The component includes built-in styling with light and dark mode support. You can customize its appearance while maintaining accessibility:

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    /* Option 1: Using :global() in your style block */
    <style>
      :global(.pagination .list) {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 1rem;
      }

      :global(.pagination a),
      :global(.pagination .disabled) {
        display: flex;
        place-items: center;
        inline-size: 2rem;
        block-size: 2rem;
        border: 2px solid;
        border-radius: 0.25rem;
      }

      :global(.pagination a) {
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(204 8% 40%), hsl(215 25% 65%));
      }
    </style>

    /* Option 2: Using is:global on the style tag */
    <style is:global>
      .pagination .list {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 1rem;
      }

      .pagination a,
      .pagination .disabled {
        display: flex;
        place-items: center;
        inline-size: 2rem;
        block-size: 2rem;
        border: 2px solid;
        border-radius: 0.25rem;
      }

      .pagination a {
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(204 8% 40%), hsl(215 25% 65%));
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <Pagination
      class="rounded-lg shadow-md"
    />
    ```

<Aside type="note" title="Style scoping">
  Astro components use scoped styles by default. To override component styles, you'll need to use either `:global()` selectors or the `is:global` directive on your style tag.

## Interactive example

See the Pagination component in action with this practical example:

<div class="not-content">
  <Pagination
    firstPage="#first"
    previousPage="#prev"
    nextPage="#next"
    lastPage="#last"
    currentPage="5"
    totalPages="12"
  />

# reduced-motion.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/reduced-motion.mdx

title: Reduced motion
description: A fully accessible reduced motion toggle that respects system preferences and disables animations for users who need them.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { ReducedMotion } from 'accessible-astro-components';
import { Icon } from 'astro-icon/components';

## Introduction

The Reduced motion component provides a toggle for enabling or disabling animations and transitions across your website. It respects the user's system `prefers-reduced-motion` preference by default, persists user choices, and exposes a global JavaScript API for programmatic control. This is essential for users with vestibular disorders, motion sensitivity, or those who simply prefer a calmer browsing experience.

## When to use

- Accessibility settings panels
- User preference controls
- Sites with significant animations
- WCAG compliance (Success Criterion 2.3.3)
- Command palette / launcher integration
- Supporting users with vestibular disorders

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <p>Click the toggle below to switch between normal and reduced motion mode:</p>
  <div style="display: flex; gap: 1rem; align-items: center; margin-top: 1rem;">
    <ReducedMotion />
    <span>Try using keyboard navigation (Tab + Enter/Space) to toggle!</span>

<Aside type="caution" title="Example component">
  The toggle here demonstrates the component but may not visually affect this documentation site since Starlight uses its own styling system.

## Usage

Learn how to implement the ReducedMotion component in your project.

```astro
---
import { ReducedMotion } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<!-- Default - respects system preference -->
<ReducedMotion />

<!-- With custom icons -->
<ReducedMotion>
  <Icon name="ion:play-outline" slot="off" />
  <Icon name="ion:pause-outline" slot="on" />
</ReducedMotion>

<!-- Force reduced motion on by default -->
<ReducedMotion initialMode="on" />

<!-- Force animations on by default (ignores system preference) -->
<ReducedMotion initialMode="off" />
```

<Aside type="tip" title="System preference">
  By default (`initialMode="auto"`), the component respects the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` system preference. Once the user interacts with the toggle, their choice is saved and takes precedence.

<Aside title="Class .reduce-motion">
  The component sets a class of `reduce-motion` on the `html` element when reduced motion mode is active. You can use this class to conditionally disable animations.

## Props

Configure the ReducedMotion component using these available props to customize its behavior and appearance.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `initialMode` | `'on' \| 'off' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | Sets the initial mode. 'auto' respects system preference |
| `label` | `string` | `'Toggle Reduced Motion'` | Accessible label for the toggle button |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Slots

The ReducedMotion component supports named slots for customizing the icons displayed in normal and reduced motion modes.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Slot | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `off` | Icon or content to display when animations are enabled |
| `on` | Icon or content to display when reduced motion is active |

## JavaScript API

The ReducedMotion component exposes a global `window.reducedMotion` API for programmatic control. This is useful for integrating with command palettes, launchers, or other UI elements.

```javascript
// Toggle reduced motion mode
window.reducedMotion.toggle()

// Enable reduced motion (disable animations)
window.reducedMotion.enable()

// Disable reduced motion (enable animations)
window.reducedMotion.disable()

// Check if reduced motion is enabled
window.reducedMotion.isEnabled() // returns boolean
```

### Events

The component dispatches a `reducemotion:change` custom event when the mode changes:

```javascript
document.addEventListener('reducemotion:change', (e) => {
  console.log('Reduced motion enabled:', e.detail.enabled)
})
```

### Launcher integration

The component automatically listens for `launcher:action` events with `action: 'toggle-reduced-motion'`, making it compatible with the [Accessible Astro Launcher](https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-launcher) out of the box.

## Accessibility

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component. The ReducedMotion component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Uses semantic button element
- Proper ARIA attributes (`aria-pressed`, `aria-label`)
- Maintains focus states
- Persists across page loads using `localStorage`
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` system preference by default
- Disables all animations and transitions when active

### Why reduced motion matters

Some users experience discomfort, dizziness, or nausea when viewing animations. This includes:

- Users with vestibular disorders
- Users with motion sensitivity
- Users with certain cognitive disabilities
- Users who simply prefer less motion

By providing this toggle, you give users control over their browsing experience.

## Styling

Make the ReducedMotion component your own with custom styling while maintaining its accessibility features.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When applying custom styles, ensure they don't compromise accessibility by maintaining sufficient color contrast and touch target sizes.

### Default reduced motion styles

The component includes global styles that disable animations when reduced motion mode is active:

```css
/* These styles are automatically applied */
.reduce-motion *,
.reduce-motion *::before,
.reduce-motion *::after {
  animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
  animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
  transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
  scroll-behavior: auto !important;
}
```

### Custom animation handling

You can also check for reduced motion in your own animations:

  <TabItem label="CSS">
    ```css
    .animated-element {
      animation: slide-in 0.3s ease-out;
    }

    /* Disable animation when reduced motion is active */
    .reduce-motion .animated-element {
      animation: none;
    }

    /* Or use the media query for CSS-only solutions */
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .animated-element {
        animation: none;
      }
    }
    ```
  <TabItem label="JavaScript">
    ```javascript
    // Check programmatically before starting animations
    if (!window.reducedMotion?.isEnabled()) {
      element.animate([
        { opacity: 0 },
        { opacity: 1 }
      ], {
        duration: 300,
        easing: 'ease-out'
      })
    }

    // Or listen for changes
    document.addEventListener('reducemotion:change', (e) => {
      if (e.detail.enabled) {
        // Stop or skip animations
        cancelAnimationFrame(animationId)
      }
    })
    ```

## Interactive examples

See the ReducedMotion component in action with these practical examples.

<Aside type="caution" title="Example component">
  The toggle here demonstrates the component but may not visually affect this documentation site.

### Default style

<div class="not-content">
  <ReducedMotion />

### With custom icons

<div class="not-content">
  <ReducedMotion>
    <Icon name="ion:flash-outline" slot="off" />
    <Icon name="ion:flash-off-outline" slot="on" />
  </ReducedMotion>

---

# skip-link.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/skip-link.mdx

title: SkipLink
description: A fully accessible skip link component that helps users bypass repetitive content and navigate directly to the main content.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { SkipLink } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The SkipLink component provides a way for keyboard and screen reader users to bypass repetitive navigation elements and jump directly to the main content. It's a crucial accessibility feature that becomes visible only when focused.

<Aside type="caution" title="Required markup">
  Your page must have either an element with `id="main-content"` or an `<h1>` element for the skip link to work properly.

## When to use

A SkipLink is essential for keyboard navigation in these scenarios:

- At the top of every page
- Before navigation menus
- On pages with repetitive content
- Content-heavy websites
- Complex navigation structures
- Any site that prioritizes keyboard accessibility

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <p>Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> once to see the skip link appear:</p>
  <div style="position: relative; border: 1px dashed #ccc; padding: 2rem; margin-top: 1rem;">
    <SkipLink />
    <p>The skip link is only visible when focused, making it unobtrusive for mouse users while remaining accessible to keyboard users. In a real page, it would allow users to bypass navigation and jump directly to the main content.</p>

## Usage

Learn how to implement the SkipLink component in your project:

```astro
---
import { SkipLink } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<SkipLink />

<!-- Target element -->
<main id="main-content">
  <h1>Page title</h1>
  <!-- Your content -->
</main>
```

<Aside type="tip" title="Best practice">
  Place the SkipLink component as the first focusable element on your page, before any navigation or content. Preferably in the `header` section of your document.

## Props

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | `string` | `'Skip to main content'` | Custom text for the skip link |
| `target` | `string` | `'#main-content'` | Target element ID to skip to |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Accessibility

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component through semantic HTML elements and proper ARIA attributes. The SkipLink component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Appears only when focused (visually hidden otherwise)
- Provides keyboard-only navigation
- Uses high contrast colors for visibility
- Clear focus indicators
- Semantic HTML structure
- Proper focus management
- Fallback to `<h1>` if main content ID is missing
- Console warning if neither target is found

## Styling

Make the SkipLink component your own while maintaining its accessibility features.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When customizing styles, ensure you maintain sufficient color contrast ratios and don't remove focus indicators.

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    /* Option 1: Using :global() in your style block */
    <style>
      :global(.skip-link a) {
        position: absolute;
        z-index: 9999;
        inset-block-start: -100vh;
        inset-inline-start: 0;
        padding-block: 1rem;
        padding-inline: 3.25rem;
        border-end-end-radius: 0.5rem;
        background: light-dark(hsl(0 0% 100%), hsl(215 25% 15%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
      }

      :global(.skip-link a:hover),
      :global(.skip-link a:focus-visible) {
        inset-block-start: 0;
        outline: 2px solid currentColor;
        outline-offset: 4px;
      }
    </style>

    /* Option 2: Using is:global on the style tag */
    <style is:global>
      .skip-link a {
        position: absolute;
        z-index: 9999;
        inset-block-start: -100vh;
        inset-inline-start: 0;
        padding-block: 1rem;
        padding-inline: 3.25rem;
        border-end-end-radius: 0.5rem;
        background: light-dark(hsl(0 0% 100%), hsl(215 25% 15%));
        color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
      }

      .skip-link a:hover,
      .skip-link a:focus-visible {
        inset-block-start: 0;
        outline: 2px solid currentColor;
        outline-offset: 4px;
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <SkipLink 
      class="absolute z-50 -top-full left-0 p-4 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-100 focus:top-0 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-offset-2"
    />
    ```

<Aside type="note" title="Style scoping">
  Astro components use scoped styles by default. To override component styles, you'll need to use either `:global()` selectors or the `is:global` directive on your style tag.

## Interactive example

See the SkipLink component in action:

<Aside type="note" title="Demo note">
  The styles for this component are changed so it's visible on the page, this is purely for demonstration purposes. Normally, it's hidden and appears on the top left corner of the page when focused.

<div class="not-content">
  <SkipLink />

# tabs.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/tabs.mdx

title: Tabs
description: A fully accessible tabs component that follows WAI-ARIA guidelines for organizing content into different sections.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Tabs as AccessibleTabs, TabsList, TabsTab, TabsPanel } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The Tabs component provides a way to organize content into different sections that can be accessed one at a time. It follows WAI-ARIA guidelines and includes full keyboard support and proper ARIA attributes.

## When to use

Use the Tabs component when you need to:

- Organize related content into sections
- Switch between different views
- Present form sections
- Display product details
- Show settings panels
- Structure dashboard sections

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <AccessibleTabs>
    <TabsList>
      <TabsTab id="quick-tab1" controls="quick-panel1" selected>First tab</TabsTab>
      <TabsTab id="quick-tab2" controls="quick-panel2">Second tab</TabsTab>
      <TabsTab id="quick-tab3" controls="quick-panel3">Third tab</TabsTab>
    </TabsList>
    <TabsPanel id="quick-panel1" labelledby="quick-tab1" selected>
      <h3>First panel</h3>
      <p>Try using the arrow keys to navigate between tabs!</p>
    </TabsPanel>
    <TabsPanel id="quick-panel2" labelledby="quick-tab2">
      <h3>Second panel</h3>
      <p>Notice how the focus management works when tabbing through.</p>
    </TabsPanel>
    <TabsPanel id="quick-panel3" labelledby="quick-tab3">
      <h3>Third panel</h3>
      <p>The component handles all the ARIA attributes automatically.</p>
    </TabsPanel>
  </AccessibleTabs>

## Usage

The Tabs component consists of four parts: the container, list wrapper, individual tabs, and their corresponding panels.

```astro
---
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTab, TabsPanel } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Tabs>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTab id="tab1" controls="panel1" selected>First tab</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab id="tab2" controls="panel2">Second tab</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab id="tab3" controls="panel3">Third tab</TabsTab>
  </TabsList>

  <TabsPanel id="panel1" labelledby="tab1" selected>
    <h2>First panel</h2>
    <p>Content for first panel</p>
  </TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel id="panel2" labelledby="tab2">
    <h2>Second panel</h2>
    <p>Content for second panel</p>
  </TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel id="panel3" labelledby="tab3">
    <h2>Third panel</h2>
    <p>Content for third panel</p>
  </TabsPanel>
</Tabs>
```

<Aside type="tip" title="Progressive enhancement">
  The component uses JavaScript for enhanced functionality but maintains a logical structure even without it.

## Props

Each component in the Tabs system accepts specific props:

### Tabs
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

### TabsList
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

### TabsTab
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Required | Unique identifier for the tab |
| `controls` | `string` | Required | ID of the panel this tab controls |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether this tab is initially selected |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

### TabsPanel
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Required | Unique identifier for the panel |
| `labelledby` | `string` | Required | ID of the tab that labels this panel |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether this panel is initially visible |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Accessibility 

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component through semantic HTML elements and proper ARIA attributes. The Tabs component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Proper ARIA roles (`tablist`, `tab`, `tabpanel`)
- Keyboard navigation:
  - Left/Right arrows to move between tabs
  - Tab/Shift+Tab for focus management
- Clear focus indicators
- Proper ARIA states (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`)
- Semantic HTML structure
- Proper focus management
- Smooth transitions (respecting reduced-motion preferences)

## Styling

Make the Tabs component your own while maintaining its accessibility features.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When customizing styles, ensure you maintain sufficient color contrast ratios and don't remove focus indicators.

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    /* Option 1: Using :global() in your style block */
    <style>
      :global(.tab) {
        flex-grow: 1;
        padding-block: 0.75rem;
        padding-inline: 1rem;
        border: 2px solid;
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
        background-color: transparent;
        color: inherit;
        font-weight: 700;
        cursor: pointer;
      }

      :global(.tab[aria-selected='true']),
      :global(.tab:hover),
      :global(.tab:focus-visible) {
        color: light-dark(hsl(0 0% 100%), hsl(215 25% 27%));
        background-color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
      }

      :global(.tab-panel) {
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        min-block-size: 10rem;
        padding: 2rem;
        border: 2px solid;
        border-color: light-dark(hsl(215 25% 27%), hsl(215 25% 89%));
        border-end-end-radius: 0.5rem;
        border-end-start-radius: 0.5rem;
      }
    </style>

    /* Option 2: Using is:global on the style tag */
    <style is:global>
      .tab {
        /* Same as above */
      }

      .tab[aria-selected='true'],
      .tab:hover,
      .tab:focus-visible {
        /* Same as above */
      }

      .tab-panel {
        /* Same as above */
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <Tabs class="w-full">
      <TabsList class="flex gap-2">
        <TabsTab 
          class="flex-1 px-4 py-2 font-bold rounded-t border-2 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-800"
          id="tab1" 
          controls="panel1" 
          selected
        >
          Tab 1
        </TabsTab>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsPanel 
        class="p-4 border-2 rounded-b min-h-[10rem]"
        id="panel1" 
        labelledby="tab1" 
        selected
      >
        Panel content
      </TabsPanel>
    </Tabs>
    ```

<Aside type="note" title="Style scoping">
  Astro components use scoped styles by default. To override component styles, you'll need to use either `:global()` selectors or the `is:global` directive on your style tag.

## Interactive example

<div class="not-content">
  <AccessibleTabs>
    <TabsList>
      <TabsTab id="example-tab1" controls="example-panel1" selected>First tab</TabsTab>
      <TabsTab id="example-tab2" controls="example-panel2">Second tab</TabsTab>
      <TabsTab id="example-tab3" controls="example-panel3">Third tab</TabsTab>
    </TabsList>
    <TabsPanel id="example-panel1" labelledby="example-tab1" selected>
      <h3>First panel</h3>
      <p>Try using the arrow keys to navigate between tabs!</p>
    </TabsPanel>
    <TabsPanel id="example-panel2" labelledby="example-tab2">
      <h3>Second panel</h3>
      <p>Notice how the focus management works when tabbing through.</p>
    </TabsPanel>
    <TabsPanel id="example-panel3" labelledby="example-tab3">
      <h3>Third panel</h3>
      <p>The component handles all the ARIA attributes automatically.</p>
    </TabsPanel>
  </AccessibleTabs>

<Aside type="note" title="Implementation note">
  The component automatically handles keyboard interactions and focus management. Use unique IDs for tabs and panels to ensure proper relationships.

# toast.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/toast.mdx

title: Toast
description: A fully accessible toast notification system with multiple variants, auto-dismiss, and a convenient JavaScript API.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Button } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The Toast component provides non-intrusive notifications that appear temporarily to inform users about the result of an action or system event. It includes a provider component that manages the toast stack and a JavaScript API for triggering toasts programmatically.

<Aside type="note" title="View transitions">
  The component automatically handles Astro's view transitions and re-initializes when navigating between pages.

## When to use

Toast notifications are ideal for:

- Success confirmations ("Changes saved")
- Error messages ("Could not connect")
- Informational updates ("New message received")
- Warnings ("Session expiring soon")
- Background process status ("Sync in progress")

<Aside type="caution" title="Not for critical actions">
  Toasts are ephemeral and may be missed. For critical information requiring user acknowledgment, use a Modal or inline Notification instead.

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; margin-block-end: 1rem;">
    <Button data-toast-demo="success" data-toast-message="Changes saved successfully." type="success">Show success</Button>
    <Button data-toast-demo="error" data-toast-message="Could not save your changes." type="error">Show error</Button>
    <Button data-toast-demo="info" data-toast-message="Your session will refresh in 2 minutes." type="info">Show info</Button>
    <Button data-toast-demo="warning" data-toast-message="Storage is almost full." type="warning">Show warning</Button>

## Usage

Learn how to implement the Toast component in your project, from basic setup to advanced configurations.

### Basic setup

Add the `ToastProvider` once in your layout (typically near the end of the body):

```astro
---
import { ToastProvider } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<html>
  <body>
    <slot />
    <ToastProvider />
  </body>
</html>
```

Then trigger toasts anywhere using the global API:

```astro
<button id="save-button">Save</button>

<script>
  document.getElementById('save-button')?.addEventListener('click', () => {
    window.toast?.success('Saved successfully.')
  })
</script>
```

### Toast variants

Use the typed helper methods for common toast types:

```javascript
// Success (green)
window.toast?.success('Changes saved.')

// Error (red)
window.toast?.error('Something went wrong.')

// Info (blue)
window.toast?.info('New updates available.')

// Warning (yellow)
window.toast?.warning('Your session will expire soon.')

// Default (neutral)
window.toast?.show({ message: 'Notification' })
```

### Persistent toasts

Set `duration: 0` to create a toast that doesn't auto-dismiss:

```javascript
window.toast?.show({
  message: 'Background sync in progress...',
  type: 'info',
  duration: 0,
})
```

### Custom duration

Override the default duration (in milliseconds) per toast:

```javascript
window.toast?.success('Quick message', 2000)  // 2 seconds
window.toast?.error('Important error', 10000) // 10 seconds
```

### Dismissing toasts

```javascript
// Dismiss a specific toast by ID
const id = window.toast?.success('Hello')
window.toast?.dismiss(id)

// Dismiss all toasts
window.toast?.dismissAll()
```

<Aside type="tip" title="Keyboard dismissal">
  Users can press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to dismiss all visible toasts.

### Positioning

Control where toasts appear using the `position` prop:

```astro
<ToastProvider position="top-center" />
```

Available positions: `bottom-right` (default), `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `top-right`, `top-left`, `top-center`.

### Stacking contexts

Render `ToastProvider` near the end of your layout body when possible. If the provider must be nested inside an element that creates a stacking context, set `portal` to move the provider to `document.body` after initialization:

```astro
<ToastProvider portal />
```

## Props

### ToastProvider

Configure the toast container using these props:

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `position` | `string` | `'bottom-right'` | Position in viewport. Options: `bottom-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `top-right`, `top-left`, `top-center` |
| `duration` | `number` | `5000` | Default auto-dismiss time in milliseconds. Set to `0` for persistent toasts |
| `maxToasts` | `number` | `5` | Maximum visible toasts. Oldest are dismissed when exceeded |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `'Notifications'` | Accessible label for the toast region |
| `zIndex` | `string \| number` | `'var(--z-index-8, 80)'` | CSS z-index value applied through `--toast-z-index` |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `false` | Moves the provider to `document.body` on initialization to escape ancestor stacking contexts |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

### Toast

Individual toast props (used internally, but useful for understanding the API):

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `message` | `string` | `'Notification'` | Toast message content |
| `type` | `string` | `'default'` | Visual variant: `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error` |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to show the dismiss button |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` | `'Dismiss notification'` | Accessible label for dismiss button (for i18n) |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

## JavaScript API

The `window.toast` object provides these methods:

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Method | Signature | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| `show` | `(options: ToastOptions) => string` | Show a toast with full options, returns toast ID |
| `success` | `(message: string, duration?: number) => string` | Show success toast |
| `error` | `(message: string, duration?: number) => string` | Show error toast |
| `info` | `(message: string, duration?: number) => string` | Show info toast |
| `warning` | `(message: string, duration?: number) => string` | Show warning toast |
| `dismiss` | `(id: string, immediate?: boolean) => void` | Dismiss specific toast |
| `dismissAll` | `() => void` | Dismiss all toasts |

### ToastOptions

```typescript
type ToastOptions = {
  message: string
  type?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'default'
  duration?: number
  dismissible?: boolean
}
```

## Events

The toast system dispatches custom events on `document`:

```javascript
// Fired when a toast is shown
document.addEventListener('toast:show', (e) => {
  console.log('Toast shown:', e.detail.id, e.detail.type, e.detail.message)
})

// Fired when a toast is dismissed
document.addEventListener('toast:dismiss', (e) => {
  console.log('Toast dismissed:', e.detail.id)
})
```

## Accessibility

Accessibility is built into the core of this component:

- **Live region**: Uses `role="log"` for polite screen reader announcements
- **Keyboard support**: Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to dismiss all toasts
- **Non-intrusive**: Toasts don't steal focus from the user's current task
- **Screen reader friendly**: Type is announced before the message (e.g., "success: Changes saved")
- **Reduced motion**: Animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
- **Dismiss button**: Each toast has an accessible dismiss button

<Aside type="note" title="Focus behavior">
  Toasts intentionally don't move focus when they appear. This prevents disrupting users who are in the middle of a task.

## Styling

Customize the Toast component while maintaining its accessibility features.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When customizing styles, ensure you maintain sufficient color contrast ratios and don't remove focus indicators.

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    <style is:global>
      .toast-provider {
        /* Adjust positioning */
        --space-l: 2rem;
      }

      .toast {
        /* Custom appearance */
        border-radius: 0.75rem;
        box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.1);
      }

      .toast.type-success {
        --color-success-bg: hsl(142 76% 95%);
        --color-success-border: hsl(142 76% 36%);
        --color-success-text: hsl(142 76% 20%);
      }

      .toast.type-error {
        --color-error-bg: hsl(0 84% 95%);
        --color-error-border: hsl(0 84% 60%);
        --color-error-text: hsl(0 84% 20%);
      }

      .toast-dismiss:focus-visible {
        outline-color: currentColor;
        outline-offset: 2px;
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <ToastProvider 
      class="[&_.toast]:rounded-xl [&_.toast]:shadow-lg"
    />
    ```

### CSS custom properties

The toast system uses these CSS custom properties for theming:

```css
/* Spacing and sizing */
--space-xs
--space-2xs
--space-l
--radius-m

/* Type-specific colors (for each type: default, info, success, warning, error) */
--color-{type}-bg
--color-{type}-border
--color-{type}-text

/* Animation */
--toast-translate
--animation-timing

/* Elevation */
--elevation-2
--toast-z-index
```

## Interactive examples

### All variants

<div class="not-content" style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem;">
  <Button data-toast-demo="default" data-toast-message="Default notification">Default</Button>
  <Button data-toast-demo="success" type="success">Success</Button>
  <Button data-toast-demo="info" type="info">Info</Button>
  <Button data-toast-demo="warning" type="warning">Warning</Button>
  <Button data-toast-demo="error" type="error">Error</Button>
  <Button data-toast-demo="dismiss-all" variant="outlined">Dismiss all</Button>

### Persistent toast

<div class="not-content">
  <Button data-toast-demo="persistent" data-toast-message="This toast will stay until dismissed.">Show persistent toast</Button>

---

# tooltip.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/tooltip.mdx

title: Tooltip
description: A tooltip component using Popover API and CSS Anchor Positioning for contextual helper text.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Tooltip } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The Tooltip component displays supplemental information in a small popup anchored to a trigger element. It uses the Popover API together with CSS Anchor Positioning, so placement and fallback behavior are handled by the browser.

<Aside type="note" title="Interaction pattern">
  This implementation is activated via a trigger button (`popovertarget`), which makes it suitable for concise helper content users intentionally reveal.

<Aside type="note" title="Modern API support and fallback strategy">
  Tooltip intentionally leans on newer platform APIs (Popover API, CSS Anchor Positioning, and `@starting-style`) to reduce custom JavaScript and align with future browser-native UI patterns. The component still uses defensive CSS behavior and robust ARIA relationships for accessibility, but some positioning and animation features remain newer and may degrade in older/other browser engines.

## When to use

Use the Tooltip component when you need to:

- Explain icon-only controls
- Add short contextual guidance near an action
- Clarify labels or terms without cluttering the UI
- Show non-critical, supplementary content

<Aside type="caution" title="Use concise content">
  Tooltips are best for short supporting text. If users need rich content or interactive controls, use a dialog or drawer instead.

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <Tooltip id="tooltip-quick-example" triggerLabel="More information">
    <span>Account status</span>
    <span slot="tooltip">Your current billing and plan status.</span>
  </Tooltip>

## Usage

Learn how to implement the Tooltip component in your project, from simple helper text to positioned variants.

### Basic usage

```astro
---
import { Tooltip } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Tooltip id="tooltip-help" triggerLabel="More information">
  Profile
  <span slot="tooltip">This is the name visible to other users.</span>
</Tooltip>
```

### Positioning

```astro
<Tooltip id="tooltip-right" position="right" triggerLabel="Open help">
  Help
  <span slot="tooltip">This tooltip appears on the right when possible.</span>
</Tooltip>
```

### Icon-only trigger

```astro
<Tooltip id="tooltip-icon" triggerLabel="Learn more about notifications">
  <span aria-hidden="true">Notifications</span>
  <span slot="tooltip">Choose when and how you receive updates.</span>
</Tooltip>
```

## Props

Configure the Tooltip component with these available props.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | - | Unique ID used to connect trigger and tooltip |
| `position` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `'top'` | Preferred tooltip position |
| `offset` | `string` | `'var(--space-2xs)'` | Distance between trigger and tooltip |
| `triggerLabel` | `string` | `undefined` | Screen reader label for icon-only or unclear trigger text |
| `showIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | Show or hide the default help icon |
| `class` | `string` | `undefined` | Additional wrapper classes |

## Accessibility

Accessibility is built into the component through semantic trigger markup and descriptive relationships:

- Semantic `<button>` trigger for keyboard interaction
- `aria-describedby` linking trigger and tooltip text
- `role="tooltip"` on the popup content
- Preserved focus visibility from native button behavior
- Reduced motion support through `prefers-reduced-motion`

<Aside type="tip" title="Accessible naming">
  Provide meaningful visible trigger text. When the trigger is icon-only or ambiguous, set `triggerLabel` so assistive technologies receive a clear accessible name.

## Styling

Make the Tooltip component your own while preserving readability and contrast.

<Aside type="caution" title="Accessibility considerations">
  When customizing styles, keep sufficient color contrast and preserve visible focus indicators on the trigger.

The component exposes CSS custom properties for spacing and animation behavior:

- `--tooltip-offset`
- `--transition-duration`
- `--transition-easing`
- `--translate-offset-x`
- `--translate-offset-y`

You can provide a custom class via the `class` prop and override styles using global selectors in your project stylesheet.

## Interactive examples

See the Tooltip component in action with common usage patterns.

### Position examples

<div class="not-content">
  <div style="display: flex; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center;">
    <Tooltip id="tooltip-top-example" triggerLabel="Info top">
      <span>Top</span>
      <span slot="tooltip">Tooltip on top (default).</span>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip id="tooltip-right-example" position="right" triggerLabel="Info right">
      <span>Right</span>
      <span slot="tooltip">Tooltip prefers the right side.</span>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip id="tooltip-left-example" position="left" triggerLabel="Info left">
      <span>Left</span>
      <span slot="tooltip">Tooltip prefers the left side.</span>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip id="tooltip-bottom-example" position="bottom" triggerLabel="Info bottom">
      <span>Bottom</span>
      <span slot="tooltip">Tooltip prefers the bottom side.</span>
    </Tooltip>

## Related components

- [Modal](/components/modal/)
- [Drawer](/components/drawer/)
- [Notification](/components/notification/)

# video.mdx

Source: https://github.com/incluud/accessible-astro-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/components/video.mdx

title: Video
description: A fully accessible video component that handles responsive video with customizable aspect ratios and loading strategies.

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Video } from 'accessible-astro-components';

## Introduction

The Video component provides a flexible way to embed videos while ensuring accessibility and proper aspect ratio handling. It includes special handling for YouTube videos to prevent keyboard traps and maintain WCAG compliance.

<Aside type="note" title="Video platform support">
  While currently optimized for YouTube embeds, we plan to add support for Vimeo, Wistia, and self-hosted videos in future releases. Want to help expand platform support? Contributions are welcome! For additional video platform options, check out [Astro Embeds](https://astro-embed.netlify.app/) by Chris Swithinbank.

<Aside type="tip" title="Accessibility first">
  Always ensure your videos include proper captions and audio descriptions. This component handles the technical accessibility aspects, but content accessibility is equally important!

## When to use

The Video component is perfect for situations where you need embedded videos:

- Product demonstrations
- Tutorial videos
- Background videos
- Video testimonials
- Course content
- Marketing materials
- YouTube embeds

## Quick example

<div class="not-content">
  <div style="max-width: 600px;">
    <Video 
      src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j8K-ESJF814"
      title="One year of Starlight: Astro's community-built documentation theme"
      ratio="16:9"
    />
    <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.9rem;">This embedded video maintains proper aspect ratio and includes accessibility features like keyboard trap prevention and proper ARIA attributes.</p>

## Usage

Learn how to implement the Video component in your project.

### Basic

```astro
---
import { Video } from 'accessible-astro-components'
---

<Video 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j8K-ESJF814"
  title="One year of Starlight: Astro's community-built documentation theme"
  ratio="16:9"
/>
```

### YouTube specific

<Aside type="note" title="YouTube keyboard handling">
  When embedding YouTube videos, the component automatically adds `&disablekb=1` to prevent YouTube's default keyboard shortcuts from interfering with your website's accessibility. If you've already included this parameter, the component will detect it and avoid duplication.

```astro
<Video 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tk1RWcasgxs&disablekb=1"
  title="Astro Together keynote in 6 minutes"
  ratio="21:9"
  loading="eager"
/>
```

## Props

Configure the Video component using these available props to customize its behavior and appearance.

<div class="props-wrapper">
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `src` | `string` | - | URL of the video (supports YouTube and direct embed URLs) |
| `title` | `string` | - | Title for the video (required for accessibility) |
| `ratio` | `'1:1' \| '4:3' \| '16:9' \| '21:9'` | `'16:9'` | Aspect ratio of the video |
| `loading` | `'lazy' \| 'eager'` | `'lazy'` | iframe loading strategy |
| `class` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes to apply |

## Accessibility

Accessibility isn't an afterthought - it's built into the core of this component through semantic HTML elements and proper ARIA attributes. The Video component is built with accessibility in mind:

- Required title attribute for screen readers
- Prevention of YouTube keyboard traps
- Maintained aspect ratios to prevent layout shift
- Proper iframe attributes for security
- Semantic HTML structure

<Aside type="caution" title="Content accessibility">
  Remember to provide captions and audio descriptions for your videos. While this component handles technical accessibility, content accessibility requires proper video production.

## Styling

Customize the Video component while maintaining its accessibility features.

  <TabItem label="Custom CSS">
    ```css
    /* Option 1: Using :global() in your style block */
    <style>
      :global(.video-wrapper) {
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        overflow: hidden;
        box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1);
      }

      :global(.video-wrapper iframe) {
        aspect-ratio: var(--ratio);
        width: 100%;
        height: 100%;
      }
    </style>

    /* Option 2: Using is:global on the style tag */
    <style is:global>
      .video-wrapper {
        border-radius: 0.5rem;
        overflow: hidden;
        box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1);
      }

      .video-wrapper iframe {
        aspect-ratio: var(--ratio);
        width: 100%;
        height: 100%;
      }
    </style>
    ```
  <TabItem label="Tailwind Classes">
    ```astro
    <Video 
      src="https://youtube.com/..."
      title="Example Video"
      class="rounded-lg overflow-hidden shadow-md"
    />
    ```

<Aside type="note" title="Style scoping">
  Astro components use scoped styles by default. To override component styles, you'll need to use either `:global()` selectors or the `is:global` directive on your style tag.

## Interactive examples

See the Video component in action with these practical examples.

### Default YouTube embed

<Video 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j8K-ESJF814"
  title="One year of Starlight: Astro's community-built documentation theme"
  ratio="16:9"
/>

### Widescreen format

<Aside type="caution" title="Clipping in thumbnails">
  Changing the aspect ratio can cause clipping in thumbnails.

<Video 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tk1RWcasgxs"
  title="Astro Together keynote in 6 minutes"
  ratio="21:9"
/>

# Clear cache and node_modules

title: Development setup
description: Technical guidelines for developing and contributing to the Accessible Astro ecosystem.

import { Aside, Steps, FileTree } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Development environment

Before you start contributing, make sure you have all the necessary tools and software installed. This will help you get up and running quickly and ensure a smooth development experience.

<Steps>
1. **Prerequisites**
   - Node.js 18.14.1 or higher
   - npm (or pnpm/Yarn)
   - Git or GitHub Desktop for example
   - A code editor (we recommend VS Code or Cursor)
   - Browser developer tools
   - Screen reader for testing

2. **Recommended VS Code extensions**
   - Astro
   - ESLint
   - Prettier
   - TypeScript
   - MDX
</Steps>

## Project structures

Understanding the project structure is crucial for effective development. Below you'll find the structure for both our component library and themes, which follow Astro's recommended practices while maintaining a clear separation of concerns.

## Development workflow

Follow these steps to set up your development environment and start contributing. Whether you're working on components, themes, or documentation, this workflow will help you stay organized and efficient.

<Steps>
1. **Setup your repository**
   ```bash
   # Clone the repository
   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/REPO-NAME.git
   cd REPO-NAME

   # Install dependencies
   npm install

   # Start development server
   npm run dev
   ```

2. **Make your changes**
   - Follow the style guide
   - Write meaningful commit messages
   - Add tests where applicable
   - Update documentation

3. **Test your changes**
   ```bash
   # Components
   npm run typecheck  # Check TypeScript
   npm run build      # Test production build

   # Themes
   npm run build      # Test production build
   npm run preview    # Test built site
   ```

4. **Submit your changes**
   ```bash
   git add .
   git commit -m "type: description"
   git push origin branch-name
   ```
</Steps>

## Coding standards

We maintain high standards for our code to ensure accessibility, maintainability, and consistency across all projects. These guidelines help us create robust and user-friendly components and themes.

### TypeScript
- Use TypeScript for all new code
- Include proper type definitions
- Document props with JSDoc comments
- Avoid `any` types

### Accessibility
- Follow [WAI-ARIA guidelines](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- Include proper ARIA attributes
- Support keyboard navigation
- Test with screen readers
- Consider color contrast
- Support reduced motion

<Aside type="note" title="Accessibility testing">
  Remember, the first rule of ARIA is "Don't use ARIA". Use it when you need to, but don't overuse it. Try to use native HTML elements and attributes first.

### CSS
- Use logical properties (inline/block)
- Follow mobile-first approach
- Support dark mode with `light-dark()`
- Use consistent border-radius (`0.5rem`)
- Use HSL colors
- Support prefers-reduced-motion
- Use `:where()` for lower specificity

<Aside type="tip" title="CSS custom properties">
  Use semantic names for variables:
  ```css
  --transition-duration: 0.2s;
  --transition-easing: cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1);
  ```

## Testing

Quality assurance is a crucial part of our development process. We focus on manual testing and accessibility validation to ensure our components and themes work well for everyone.

### Components
- Manual accessibility testing
- TypeScript validation
- Browser testing
- Screen reader testing
- Keyboard navigation testing
- Reduced motion testing

### Themes
- Cross-browser testing
- Responsive testing
- Performance testing
- Accessibility validation
- Dark mode testing
- Screen reader testing
- Keyboard navigation testing

## Common issues

During development, you might encounter some common issues. Here are some solutions that can help you resolve them quickly and get back to coding.

### Build errors
```bash
# Clear cache and node_modules
npm run clean
rm -rf node_modules
npm install
```

### Type errors
- Check prop types
- Update type definitions
- Run typecheck command

<Aside type="caution" title="Breaking changes">
  Major changes require:
  - Documentation updates
  - Migration guides
  - Version bump
  - Changelog entry

## Resources

These resources will help you better understand our technical stack and accessibility requirements. We recommend bookmarking them for future reference.

- [Astro documentation](https://docs.astro.build)
- [WAI-ARIA practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [WCAG guidelines](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
- [TypeScript handbook](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook)
- [Modern CSS guide](https://moderncss.dev)
